gen-gf-francois-one-fs-karma: Francois One has big-bodied lowercase with curves that barely open, a dense and confident look. Karma follows with a gentle modulation and terminals held clear of the stem, so the serif feels trustworthy beside it.
gen-gf-fresca-fs-erode: Modern, with a single thick thread tracing each letter in Fresca. It simply draws clean, open curves, while Erode, a text serif, brings dignity through its tall middle band and softly shifting stroke weight.
gen-gf-fresca-fs-karma: Contemporary lines in Fresca run as one unbroken thread, with capitals only slightly taller than the lowercase around them. Karma adds classic warmth.
gen-gf-funnel-sans-fs-erode: Funnel Sans draws its letters with a wire-like line, curves left open instead of pinching shut. And Erode, a text serif, brings a reed-pen thickening and a tall middle band that feels editorial beside it.
gen-gf-funnel-sans-fs-karma: Karma reads as trustworthy and classic, its serif arches thinning a touch as they leave the stem. Funnel Sans is best at ruler-straight, open-curved lines, whereas Karma does its best work in quiet, tightly set text.
gen-gf-gabarito-bitter: Bitter reads dependable and grounded, with a very large lowercase eye and a visible gap in each s. Bitter, a slab-serif, would keep a long passage steady, while Gabarito's one-nib display letters supply the expression above it.
gen-gf-gabarito-instrument-sans: Expressive from the first line, Gabarito looks drawn with a single nib. Instrument Sans, a plain sans, then settles in below with c ends pointing apart like pincers and a minimal step from capital to lowercase.
gen-gf-gabarito-inter: Loud up top, smooth below. Gabarito does best with its open, one-nib display letters, whereas Inter, a plain sans, is built for tube-like lines with big counters in a tall lowercase.
gen-gf-gabarito-mulish: Gabarito is drawn with one nib, its terminals cut open so the counters flow outward. Mulish, a sans-serif, has no thickness shifts at all, so a small heading would lose that expressive edge next to its large x-height.
gen-gf-gabarito-poppins: Distinctive is the right word for Gabarito, with its one-nib look and openly cut terminals. Poppins, a plain sans, brings loose curves and a sturdy tall lowercase, and the gap in lowercase height between them is the real strength.
